access.closures: The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen is closed until further notice to both vehicle and foot traffic — crossing there is prohibited and you must use a staffed port of entry. As of 24 July 2026 the Silver-Skagit Road was also closed at km 6 for the Border 2 Fire. Verify both before committing to a trip.

road.name: Silver-Skagit Road (Skagit Valley Road) from Hope, British Columbia
road.status: Unpaved for its full ~37 miles / 60 km. Maintained and graded periodically, but washboard and potholes are the norm and every source advises carrying a spare tire. Rebuilt after the 2021 B.C. flood washouts. As of 24 July 2026 DriveBC listed it CLOSED at km 6, past Silver Lake, because the Border 2 Fire - burning 2.4 km east of Hozomeen in Washington - had crossed the border into British Columbia.
road.driveNote: Trans-Canada Hwy 1 Exit 168 at Hope, then Flood-Hope Road to Silver-Skagit Road and south on gravel. About 1 to 1.5 hours to the far end. Skyline II trailhead is near km 55 (about 34 miles in); Hozomeen Campground and the Hozomeen Lake trailhead are at the very end. A passenger car handles it when freshly graded; ground clearance helps when it is not.
road.seasonalGate: B.C. closes Silver-Skagit Road for a seasonal winter shutdown, posted for 15 October 2025 to 14 April 2026. Separately and more importantly, the NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen is closed until further notice, with vehicle and foot traffic across the border there prohibited; the crossing has never been staffed and is camera-monitored.

access.fees: No entrance fee for the North Cascades National Park Complex. Hozomeen Campground is free and first-come, first-served, typically open late May through October. Backcountry permits are $10 per person plus a $6 reservation fee; ages 15 and under are free.
access.permit: An NPS wilderness/backcountry permit is required for any overnight camp in the complex, including the cross-country zones on Hozomeen. Reserve on Recreation.gov - an early-access lottery governs the 15 May to 10 October peak season and roughly 40% of capacity is held back for walk-ups - then watch the mandatory safety video and email noca_wilderness@nps.gov no more than three days before departure to receive the permit. A pure day climb needs no permit. Bear canisters are required in some zones and must be collected in person at Marblemount or Glacier.
access.closures: The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen is closed until further notice; vehicle and foot traffic across the US/Canada border there is prohibited and visitors must use a designated port of entry. As of 24 July 2026 Silver-Skagit Road itself was closed at km 6 for the Border 2 Fire. Confirm both with NPS and DriveBC before committing to the trip.
access.landManager: National Park Service - Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades National Park Complex (peak and all US-side approaches). The drive in crosses B.C. Parks' Skagit Valley Provincial Park. NPS complex information line 360-854-7200.
access.passRequired: No Northwest Forest Pass or Discover Pass. You do need a passport or NEXUS card, because the entire drive is through Canada and you must enter and re-enter the US at a staffed port of entry - Hozomeen is not one.

Closed at km 6 as of 24 July 2026 for the Border 2 Fire, which crossed into B.C. from Washington 2.4 km east of Hozomeen.
road.driveNote: Hwy 1 Exit 168 at Hope, Flood-Hope Road, then Silver-Skagit Road south to its end at Hozomeen. About 1 to 1.5 hours. This route starts at the very end of the road at the ranger station, so the border-gate closure blocks it completely when in force.
road.seasonalGate: B.C. seasonal winter shutdown posted 15 October 2025 to 14 April 2026. The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen is separately closed until further notice to both vehicles and foot traffic.

access.fees: No park entrance fee. Hozomeen Campground is free and first-come, first-served, late May through October. Backcountry permits $10 per person plus $6 reservation fee; 15 and under free.
access.permit: No permit needed for a day climb, which is how this route is usually done. Any overnight bivouac on the ridge requires an NPS wilderness permit for the relevant cross-country zone, reserved through Recreation.gov and issued by email after the safety video, or picked up in person at Marblemount.
access.closures: NPS border gate at Hozomeen closed until further notice to vehicle and foot traffic. Silver-Skagit Road closed at km 6 as of 24 July 2026 for the Border 2 Fire. Both must be verified before the trip.

access.fees: No park entrance fee. Backcountry permits $10 per person plus a $6 reservation fee; 15 and under free. Hozomeen Campground is free and first-come, first-served, late May through October.
access.permit: An NPS wilderness permit is required for the camp north of the peak and for any bivouac, including one on the wall. Reserve through Recreation.gov, complete the safety video, and email noca_wilderness@nps.gov within three days of departure, or pick up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center. Build slack into your permitted nights - this route reliably takes longer than planned.
access.closures: NPS border gate at Hozomeen closed until further notice to vehicle and foot traffic. Silver-Skagit Road closed at km 6 as of 24 July 2026 for the Border 2 Fire.

access.fees: $10 per person, per night backcountry camping fee, charged mid-May through early October (no charge the rest of the year); $6 non-refundable Recreation.gov reservation/lottery fee per permit application.
access.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: No cell service at Ross Lake/Hozomeen; pack out all trash (no services at Hozomeen Campground); Ross Lake water taxi requires advance reservation.
access.permit: Overnight backcountry permit required year-round for any camping en route (e.g., Lightning Creek, Hozomeen Campground, or high camps). Obtain at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount or reserve in advance via Recreation.gov (about 60% of backcountry sites are reservable; the rest are walk-up, first-come, first-served and can be competitive at Ross Lake in summer). Reserved permits must be picked up by 11:00 AM PT on the trip start date or the reservation may be cancelled.
access.closures: The US/Canada border crossing at Hozomeen (used for the historic Silver Skagit Road approach from Hope, BC) has been closed to both vehicle and foot traffic since the COVID-19 pandemic and remains closed as of 2026.
access.landManager: North Cascades National Park Service Complex / Ross Lake National Recreation Area (NPS)
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP wilderness permit for the lake and cross-country camps; none for the drive-in campground
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov or get one at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center before the trip. Hozomeen Campground itself is first come, first served.

access.fees: No climbing or parking fee; the NPS wilderness permit for Ross Lake NRA camps carries a fee.
access.rules: USFS wilderness group-size limits apply once inside Pasayten Wilderness (max 12 people/18 head of stock). The lower Lightning Creek/Freezeout Creek approach corridor lies within Ross Lake National Recreation Area (North Cascades National Park Service Complex) before crossing into Pasayten Wilderness (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF); NPS regulations (designated-camp food storage, campfire restrictions at elevation, etc.) govern that stretch. Pack out all waste; practice Leave No Trace.
access.permit: Overnight camping on the Ross Lake NRA portion of the approach (Lightning Creek Trail) requires an NPS backcountry/wilderness permit, reservable in advance on Recreation.gov ($6 reservation fee plus $10/person/night camping fee, ages 15 and under free) or picked up as a walk-up at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount. Once past the wilderness boundary into the Pasayten Wilderness (USFS) portion, a free self-issued wilderness permit applies. If approaching via Manning Park/Monument 78, crossing into the US on foot outside a sanctioned port of entry is not lawful; there is no permit for entering the US on the trail, so parties cannot walk across at the monument.
access.closures: NPS reports the Hozomeen border gate is CLOSED — vehicle and foot traffic across the US/Canada border there is prohibited until further notice, closing off the Silver-Skagit Road driving approach. On the Canadian side, Silver-Skagit Road also has a seasonal closure roughly Oct 15-Apr 14.
access.landManager: Mixed jurisdiction: Ross Lake National Recreation Area / North Cascades National Park Service Complex (NPS) on the lower Lightning Creek approach, transitioning into Pasayten Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District) for the upper mountain and summit.
access.parking_pass: None needed at the Ross Dam trailhead.
access.passRequired: No Northwest Forest Pass is needed at the NPS Ross Lake trailheads — a paid NPS wilderness permit (Recreation.gov) is required there instead. A Northwest Forest Pass may be needed for parking if using a USFS trailhead on the PCT/Manning Park approach option.

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP complex backcountry permit for Ross Lake NRA camps; free self-issue Pasayten permit beyond
overnight_permit.where: Reserve Ross Lake and Lightning Creek camps on Recreation.gov or get a walk-up permit at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center. Past the Pasayten Wilderness boundary, fill out a free self-issue permit.

road.name: Harts Pass Road (Forest Road 5400)
road.status: Closed indefinitely since Dec 2025 flood/storm damage; conflicting June 2026 reports on reopening — verify directly with the Methow Valley Ranger District before travel
road.driveNote: Even when open, it's WA's highest drivable pass (6,198 ft) — narrow, rugged, high-clearance recommended. There is no lawful alternative: walking south into the US on the PCT from Manning Provincial Park, BC is not a legal border crossing, so this road is the only way in.
road.seasonalGate: Generally open through summer into September/October depending on snowpack; may be briefly gated on weekdays during periodic summer gravel-hauling/maintenance work

access.fees: None — no entrance fee; the required wilderness permit is free.
access.rules: Leave No Trace; Pasayten Wilderness caps groups at 12 people and stock combined (larger groups must split and stay a mile apart); grizzly bear and gray wolf habitat — store food properly; weed-free feed required for stock.
access.permit: Free, non-quota, self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead (required for overnight use); no advance reservation.
access.closures: Harts Pass Road (FS Road 5400) sustained major damage in Dec 2025 storms/flooding and was closed indefinitely from the Monument Creek Trailhead through Harts Pass, cutting off the Robinson, Rattlesnake, Harts Pass, Brown Bear, Slate Pass, and Slate Peak trailheads. USFS targeted an 'early summer' 2026 reopening; as of mid-late June 2026 reports conflicted (one tracker listed it reopened, USFS estimated mid-July) — call the Methow Valley Ranger District at (509) 996-4000 to confirm current status before relying on Harts Pass access.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Harts Pass approach).
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.
access.passRequired: No pass required at the Harts Pass Trailhead itself; some other Okanogan-Wenatchee NF trailheads in the area require a Northwest Forest Pass, so check trailhead kiosks.

overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the Harts Pass trailhead kiosk before walking in.

road.name: Harts Pass Road (Forest Road 5400)
road.status: Closed indefinitely as of spring 2026 due to storm damage; USFS was targeting an early-summer reopening (unconfirmed) — verify before travel.
road.driveNote: Narrow, unpaved, and exposed in sections near Slate Peak — high-clearance recommended; not plowed or maintained in winter.
road.seasonalGate: In a normal year the road is snow-gated roughly late October/November through late June-early July; Harts Pass Campground typically operates July-September.

access.fees: No wilderness entry fee. The developed Harts Pass Trailhead (vault toilet) may require a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass for parking; the more rustic Slate Peak/Slate Pass and Monument Creek trailheads typically aren't fee sites, but carrying a pass is a safe bet.
access.rules: Standard Pasayten Wilderness group-size limits apply; use bear-resistant food storage given the 2024-approved North Cascades grizzly bear reintroduction effort, which covers the Pasayten.
access.permit: Free, non-quota, self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead — no reservation or quota system for the Pasayten Wilderness.
access.closures: Harts Pass Road (FR 5400) — the primary access road for all standard approaches — was closed indefinitely by the Forest Service in spring 2026 after storm damage, with USFS targeting an early-summer reopening that was unconfirmed. Verify current road status with the Methow Valley Ranger District / Okanogan-Wenatchee NF before planning a trip.
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.

overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead registration box. No reservation is needed.

road.name: Holden Village access (boat + shuttle) — currently closed
road.driveNote: No direct road access; normally reached via the Lady of the Lake ferry up Lake Chelan plus a shuttle to Holden Village. As of 2026, Holden Village and Forest Road 8301 are closed indefinitely (2025 flood/landslide damage, not expected to reopen before 2027 per USFS/Holden Village), so the remaining line is the Phelps Creek Trailhead over Spider Gap. That is not a drive-to alternative either: FR 6200 is gated at milepost 18.2 past Atkinson Flat under USFS order #06-17-07-2026-11, cutting off both the Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads, so the Spider Gap approach itself now begins with several miles of closed road.

approach: Standard approach is via Holden Village: Lady of the Lake ferry from Chelan or Fields Point Landing to Lucerne, shuttle to Holden, then roughly 8 miles up the Railroad Creek Trail to Lyman Lake. As of 2026, Holden Village and Forest Road 8301 are closed to all hikers and vehicles due to 2025 flood/landslide damage, with reopening not expected before 2027 at the earliest — the only current access to Lyman Lake is the longer Phelps Creek Trailhead approach over Spider Gap (roughly 11–12 miles one-way, glacier travel with ice axe required).
